'''Eugenia Loh-Gene Cheng''' is a British mathematician, educator and concert pianist. Her mathematical interests include [[higher category theory]], and as a pianist she specialises in [[lied]]er and [[art song]].<ref name="sheffieldpiano">{{cite web|url=http://cheng.staff.shef.ac.uk/piano/|title=Eugenia Cheng, piano|publisher=cheng.staff.shef.ac.uk|accessdate=12 August 2015|archive-date=18 September 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150918052744/http://cheng.staff.shef.ac.uk/piano/|url-status=dead}}</ref> She is also known for explaining mathematics to non-mathematicians to combat [[math phobia]], often using analogies with food and baking.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2016/05/03/science/eugenia-cheng-math-how-to-bake-pi.html|title=Eugenia Cheng Makes Math a Piece of Cake|first=Natalie|last=Angier |newspaper=The New York Times|date=2 May 2010|access-date=26 September 2016}}</ref> Cheng is a [[Artist-in-residence|scientist-in-residence]] at the [[School of the Art Institute of Chicago]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite magazine|last=Klinkenberg|first=Brendan|date=May 2015|title=The Perfect Recipe|magazine=WIRED|page=24}}</ref><ref name="chicago">{{cite web|url=http://www.saic.edu/profiles/faculty/eugeniacheng/|title=SAIC – Eugenia Cheng – School of the Art Institute of Chicago|publisher=saic.edu|accessdate=12 August 2015}}</ref><ref name="about">{{cite web |url= http://eugeniacheng.com/math/about/  |title=About |website=Eugenia Cheng |accessdate=28 July 2020}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Cheng was born in [[Hampshire]], England. She moved to [[Sussex]] at the age of one.<ref name="times">{{cite web|url=https://www.timeshighereducation.co.uk/content/book-review-cakes-custard-and-category-theory-by-eugenia-cheng|title=Cakes, Custard and Category Theory: Easy Recipes for Understanding Complex Maths, by Eugenia Cheng &#124; Times Higher Education|date=4 June 2015|publisher=timeshighereducation.co.uk|accessdate=12 August 2015}}</ref> Her family is originally from [[Hong Kong]].<ref name="Chinese name">{{Cite web|url=http://eugeniacheng.com/pronunciation/|title = Pronunciation}}</ref> Her interest in mathematics stemmed from a young age thanks largely to her mother who made mathematics a part of life.<ref name="times" /><ref name="medium">{{cite web|title=Why I Don't Like Being a "Female Role Model" — Bright – Medium|url=https://medium.com/bright/why-i-don-t-like-being-a-female-role-model-10055873ea97|author=Dr Eugenia Cheng|website=Medium.com|accessdate=12 August 2015}}</ref>

Cheng attended [[Roedean School]].<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Faberij de Jonge|first1=Jane|title=Profile: Dr Eugenia Cheng|journal=Roedean Magazine|year=2013|pages=36–37|url=http://issuu.com/roedeanschool/docs/roedean_magazine_2013_final_single_/39}}</ref> She studied the [[Mathematical Tripos]] at the [[University of Cambridge]], where she was a student of [[Gonville and Caius College, Cambridge]]. Her postgraduate research was supervised by [[Martin Hyland]].<ref name=mathgene/><ref name=ePhD>{{cite thesis|degree=PhD|publisher=University of Cambridge|url=http://cheng.staff.shef.ac.uk/thesis.pdf|title=Higher-dimensional category theory : opetopic foundations|first= Eugenia Loh-Gene|last=Cheng|year=2002|id={{EThOS|uk.bl.ethos.597569}}|website=cheng.staff.shef.ac.uk|oclc=879393286|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081031182847/http://cheng.staff.shef.ac.uk/thesis.pdf|archive-date=31 October 2008}}</ref><ref name="ChengHyland2003">{{cite journal|last1=Cheng|first1=Eugenia|last2=Hyland|first2=Martin|last3=Power|first3=John|title=Pseudo-distributive Laws|journal=[[Electronic Notes in Theoretical Computer Science]]|volume=83|year=2003|pages=227–245|issn=1571-0661|doi=10.1016/S1571-0661(03)50012-3|doi-access=free}}</ref>

==Career and research==
As of 2020, Cheng is a scientist-in-residence at the School of the Art Institute of Chicago, where she teaches mathematics to arts students.<ref name=":0" /><ref name="about"/> Cheng formerly held academic appointments at the [[University of Nice Sophia Antipolis]], the [[University of Sheffield]] and the [[University of Chicago]].<ref name="about"/>

She has published over a dozen research papers across several journals within her area of category theory.<ref name="shef">{{cite web|url=http://cheng.staff.shef.ac.uk/research.html|title=Research papers|publisher=cheng.staff.shef.ac.uk|accessdate=12 August 2015|archive-date=21 October 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151021064210/http://cheng.staff.shef.ac.uk/research.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> 

=== Mathematics and baking ===
Cheng's research interests are in [[category theory]], which she has written about for a general audience by using analogies from baking. Her vision is to rid the world of mathematics phobia. In ''[[How to Bake Pi]]'', published on May 5, 2015,<ref name=":0" /> each chapter begins with a recipe for a dessert, to illustrate the commonalities in the methods and principles of mathematics and cooking. The book was well received<ref name="times" /><ref>
{{cite web |url=https://www.kirkusreviews.com/book-reviews/eugenia-cheng/how-to-bake-pi/ |title='How to Bake Pi: An Edible Exploration of the Mathematics of Mathematics' by Eugenia Cheng |date=15 March 2015 |work=[[Kirkus Reviews]]|accessdate=26 September 2016 }}</ref><ref>
{{cite news |last=Bellos |first=Alex|author-link=Alex Bellos |date=12 June 2015 |title='How to Bake Pi,' by Eugenia Cheng |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2015/06/14/books/review/how-to-bake-pi-by-eugenia-cheng.html |newspaper=[[The New York Times]] |location=New York City |accessdate=13 June 2015 }}
</ref> and has since been translated into French.<ref>
{{cite book
|title=Comment cuire un 9
|first=Eugenia
|last=Cheng
|publisher=Flammarion
|url=http://editions.flammarion.com/Albums_Detail.cfm?ID=49375&levelCode=home
|isbn=978-2-08-138213-8
|translator-first=Olivier
|translator-last=Courcelle
|date=2016}}</ref>

Cheng has also written a number of papers with similar themes, such as ''On the perfect quantity of cream for a scone''<ref>{{cite web|url=http://cheng.staff.shef.ac.uk/misc/cheng-cream.pdf|title=On the perfect quantity of cream for a scone|author=Eugenia Cheng|website=Cheng.staff.shef.ac.uk|accessdate=24 January 2018|archive-date=27 April 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180427223922/http://cheng.staff.shef.ac.uk/misc/cheng-cream.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref> and ''On the perfect size for a pizza''.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://cheng.staff.shef.ac.uk/misc/cheng-pizza.pdf|title=On the perfect size for a pizza|author=Eugenia Cheng|website=Cheng.staff.shef.ac.uk|accessdate=24 January 2018|archive-date=31 October 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171031201823/http://cheng.staff.shef.ac.uk/misc/cheng-pizza.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref> Cheng has presented similar topics through YouTube in a light-hearted manner and has explored mathematics in other ways such as in her speech ''Mathematics and Lego: the untold story''.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://cheng.staff.shef.ac.uk/misc/pud2.pdf|title=Mathematics and Lego : the untold story|author=Eugenia Cheng|website=Cheng.staff.shef.ac.uk|accessdate=24 January 2018|archive-date=4 March 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304190222/http://cheng.staff.shef.ac.uk/misc/pud2.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref>

=== Other writing ===
Cheng's second book, ''[[Beyond Infinity (mathematics book)|Beyond Infinity]]'', explains [[set theory]] for lay audiences using analogies and anecdotes, including [[Cantor's diagonal argument]] and [[Zeno's paradoxes]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://euro-math-soc.eu/review/beyond-infinity-expedition-outer-limits-mathematics|title=Review: Beyond Infinity: An Expedition to the Outer Limits of Mathematics {{!}} EMS|website=euro-math-soc.eu|access-date=13 October 2018}}</ref> It was shortlisted for the 2017 Insight Investment Science Book Prize under the [[Royal Society Prizes for Science Books]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://royalsociety.org/grants-schemes-awards/book-prizes/science-book-prize/2017/|title=2017 Royal Society Insight Investment Science Book Prize {{!}} Royal Society|website=royalsociety.org|access-date=13 October 2018}}</ref>

She published her third book, ''The Art of Logic in an Illogical World,'' in 2018.<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://www.basicbooks.com/titles/eugenia-cheng/the-art-of-logic-in-an-illogical-world/9781541672482/|title=The Art of Logic in an Illogical World|date=16 January 2018|isbn=9781541672482|language=en-US|last1=Cheng|first1=Eugenia |publisher=Basic Books }}</ref> It explores arguments on real-world topics like [[same-sex marriage]], [[white privilege]], and [[police brutality in the United States]] using methods from [[logic]], including explanations of [[Russell's paradox]] and [[Euclid's axioms]] on the way.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/books/2018/jul/19/the-art-of-logic-by-eugenia-cheng-review|title=The Art of Logic by Eugenia Cheng review – the need for good arguments|last=Guest|first=Katy|date=19 July 2018|website=The Guardian|access-date=13 October 2018}}</ref>

Cheng writes the column ''Everyday Math'' for ''[[The Wall Street Journal]]''<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.wsj.com/news/author/8737|title=Eugenia Cheng - News, Articles, biography, Photos |website=The Wall Street Journal|access-date=13 October 2018}}</ref> on topics including [[probability theory]], [[set theory]] and [[Rubik's Cube]] solutions.

=== Music ===
Cheng is a pianist who specialises in [[lieder]] and [[art song]]. She was awarded the Sheila Mossman Memorial Award from the [[Associated Board of the Royal Schools of Music]] and was the first recipient of the Brighton and Hove Arts Council Award for the Musician of the Year.  In Chicago, she gave a recital in the Pianoforte Chicago recital series; she performed ''[[Schwanengesang]]'' and ''[[Winterreise]]'' with [[Paul Giger|Paul Geiger]] at Schubertiade Chicago in 2005 and 2006 respectively, and ''[[Die Schöne Müllerin]]'' with Ryan de Ryke at Schubertiade Chicago 2007. She performed lieder with tenor Nicholas Harkness in the Noontime Recital Series at the University of Chicago, the Salon Series at the Tower Club, and the Maxwell Recital Series, and she gave recitals for the Auxiliary Board Chapter of the Lyric Opera; she also performed ''[[La Traviata]]'' at the Oak Park Village Players.<ref>{{cite web|title = Eugenia Cheng, piano|url = http://cheng.staff.shef.ac.uk/piano|website = cheng.staff.shef.ac.uk|accessdate = 4 November 2015|archive-date = 18 September 2015|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20150918052744/http://cheng.staff.shef.ac.uk/piano/|url-status = dead}}</ref>

In 2013, Cheng founded the Liederstube as an oasis for art song in the Fine Arts Building, in downtown Chicago.  The mission of the Liederstube is to present and enjoy classical music in an intimate and informal setting. The Liederstube is a Not For Profit [[501(c)(3)]] organisation.<ref>{{cite web|title = home|url = http://liederstube.wix.com/home|website =Liederstube.wix.com|accessdate = 4 November 2015}}</ref>

===Media appearances===
Cheng has appeared on ''[[The Late Show with Stephen Colbert]]'' making [[mille-feuille]] with [[Stephen Colbert]] in 2015 to demonstrate [[Exponential function|exponentials]].<ref>{{Citation|last=The Late Show with Stephen Colbert|title=Dr. Eugenia Cheng Gives Paula Deen A Run For Her Butter|date=5 November 2015|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mA402F5K47o|accessdate=2 March 2017}}</ref> She was interviewed for the morning magazine show ''The Morning Shift'' on Chicago's [[Public Radio]] station ''[[WBEZ]]'' in 2017.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.wbez.org/shows/morning-shift-podcast/eugenia-cheng-math-is-about-discovery-not-right-or-wrong/6e5544ac-198d-4b09-8cb9-31dbfd3f13fd|title=Eugenia Cheng: Math Is About Discovery|publisher=WBEZ|access-date=13 October 2018}}</ref> She was interviewed by [[Jim Al-Khalili]] for ''[[The Life Scientific]]'' on [[BBC Radio 4]], first broadcast in January 2018.<ref name=tls>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/b09nvrcn|title=Eugenia Cheng on the mathematics of mathematics|first=Jim|last=Al-Khalili|year=2018|publisher=BBC|location=London}}</ref> She appeared on the [[WGBH (FM)|WGBH]] podcast ''[[Innovation Hub (radio program)|Innovation Hub]]'' in spring 2018.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://blogs.wgbh.org/innovation-hub/2018/5/4/full-show-spoonful-sugar/|title=Recent Entries|website=Innovation Hub {{!}} WGBH.org Blogs|access-date=13 October 2018}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Cheng met her partner, Peter “Pete” Wesoloski, when she was 39. In a 2024 ''Wall Street Journal'' article, Cheng wrote about her fertility issues and childlessness.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Cheng |first=Eugenia |date=2024-08-30 |title=Essay {{!}} I Am Childless, but Not by Choice |url=https://www.wsj.com/lifestyle/relationships/i-am-childless-but-not-by-choice-730bfd68 |access-date=2025-01-28 |website=Wall Street Journal |language=en-US}}</ref>
